title: Internet activity and jurisdiction
summary: Internet-jurisdiction questions ask which online activities connect a particular defendant to a particular forum. The ability to access a site everywhere creates a need to identify meaningful forum-directed conduct.
notes: Website interactivity alone is not a universal Supreme Court test. The selected source is a casebook account and accompanying notes, not an endorsement of jurisdiction wherever a site can be viewed.

sections.How to work through the question: Read the transactions, subscribers, communications, and commercial activity actually linked to the state. Zippo’s sliding scale is one lower-court approach described in the reading; the surrounding notes compare later attention to purposeful activity and the claim.
